title: Effectiveness of a Generate→Validate→Repair Pipeline with Batfish for Intent-to-Configuration Translation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a sealed paired confirmatory study (CNSM2026-GenVal-Batfish-PR-v1) to measure whether inserting a deterministic Batfish-style validator into a bounded generate→validate→repair pipeline reduces validator-detected deployment-risk configuration errors produced by an LLM intent-to-configuration translator. The preregistered contract used shared_initial_generation (one initial model generation per task reused by both baseline and guarded conditions) to isolate repair-mediated differences from generator sampling variance. Under this contract we ran 200 paired tasks (50 per prespecified stratum: IOS-like single-step, IOS-like multi-step, JunOS-like single-step, JunOS-like multi-step) using the declared generator gpt-5-mini and a bounded repair budget (≤1 repair attempt per task). Execution artifacts show both arms were validator-clean on every task (baseline = 200/200, guarded = 200/200), giving a paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0, paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples; bootstrap seed archived), and exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. No repairs were invoked (repair count = 0), so the preregistered secondary estimand (repair_success_rate > 50%) is not empirically computable. We reconcile this degenerate null with respect to the preregistered contract, give concise validator semantics used to define the primary outcome, supply explicit artifact-grounded reproducibility pointers, and discuss construct/internal/external validity implications and targeted follow-ups supported by the archived bundle.

sections.introduction: Automating intent-to-configuration translation promises productivity gains for network operations but also raises acute safety concerns: an incorrect command can create outages, violate policies, or introduce routing instability. A common mitigation is a generate→validate→repair loop that places a deterministic verifier (sandbox) between model generation and deployment. Prior work argues for verifier-in-the-loop workflows and layered controls, yet controlled quantification isolating the verifier’s marginal benefit (repair-mediated improvements) from generator sampling variance is limited. We therefore preregistered CNSM2026-GenVal-Batfish-PR-v1 to answer: does integrating a deterministic Batfish-like validator into a bounded generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce validator-detected deployment-risk configuration errors compared to LLM-only generation when initial candidate generation is shared between arms (shared_initial_generation)? The main contributions are: (1) a sealed paired-trial using shared_initial_generation to attribute any paired discordance to repair activity; (2) a fully archived execution of 200 paired tasks across four balanced strata with deterministic per-episode validator traces; and (3) an artifact-grounded interpretation of a degenerate null outcome, together with reproducible, targeted follow-ups that vary generation independence, repair budget, and validator fidelity.
sections.related_work: LLM-driven NetOps research spans intent-driven configuration synthesis, verifier-assisted repair, and agentic orchestration frameworks. Representative experimental work has demonstrated intent-driven synthesis prototypes and in-context approaches for vendor-like targets (Nguyen Tu et al., 2024; Wei et al., 2025). Generate→validate→repair and bounded self-correction patterns have been proposed as primary mitigations for unsafe outputs (Sang 2025; Okula 2026). Surveys and architecture papers emphasize workflow-centred evaluation, human gates, and sandbox verification (Bilal et al., 2026; Malik 2026). Rising literature also develops failure-mode taxonomies and runtime defenses advocating layered controls and traceability (Maharaj 2026; Vadlamudi 2026). Our work differs methodologically: we preregistered a single confirmatory estimand in a paired design, enforced shared_initial_generation to isolate repair effects, and archived deterministic validator traces and reconciliation artifacts to enable reproducible interpretation. The cited works demonstrate the breadth of proposals and prototypes but leave open controlled, artifact-grounded comparisons that isolate repair-mediated gains under constrained repair budgets.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand: The study was preregistered and sealed prior to execution as CNSM2026-GenVal-Batfish-PR-v1 (preregistration_sha256: aa4055d52c118741524c4c42d07efa977372be338b9bd96069dc7abfc5b32ac4). The primary estimand is the paired absolute difference in per-task validator-clean rate (guarded − baseline), where a task is 'validator-clean' when the deterministic validator reports zero violations on the final configuration. The confirmatory test is an exact McNemar two-sided test (α=0.05) and paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CIs with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed archived). Design and sampling: We used a paired binary design with 200 distinct intent-to-configuration tasks. Tasks were balanced across four prespecified strata (50 tasks each): IOS-like single-step, IOS-like multi-step, JunOS-like single-step, JunOS-like multi-step. These per-stratum counts were enforced by the deterministic task generator and are recorded in the archived task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl, sha256: 4e8aa65489313209485a8492fb890be771570c0c487a6cb8da7b55db3fc1a39b). Shared-initial-generation contract and rationale: To attribute differences specifically to repair activity, we produced one initial generation per task and reused that candidate for both baseline and guarded evaluations (initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1). This removes generator-sampling variance as a cause of paired discordance: any discordant pair must result from repair actions. This preregistered trade-off increases causal clarity about repair effects but reduces the chance that generation variance will produce failing baseline samples and thus reduces empirical opportunity for repair to act.
sections.results: Execution accounting and primary outcome: The run completed the preregistered 400 episodes (200 tasks × 2 conditions) with zero failed episodes (execution manifest: started_at_utc 2026-08-28T11:15:20.528566+00:00, completed_at_utc 2026-08-28T11:37:01.389670+00:00; completed_episode_count = 400; failed_episode_count = 0). Provider accounting matched the shared-initial contract: model_calls_used = 200 (one initial call per task), maximum_model_calls permitted = 400. Aggregated scoring artifacts indicate baseline validator-clean = 200/200 and guarded validator-clean = 200/200. The four-cell paired contingency is n_11 = 200 (both-clean), n_10 = 0 (guarded-only-clean), n_01 = 0 (baseline-only-clean), n_00 = 0 (both-error). Point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples; archived seed) 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0]. These aggregated results and the contingency table are provided as analysis artifacts (analysis/condition_summary.csv sha256: 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv sha256: 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c). Repair activity: Because validator-detected errors never occurred on any shared initial candidate, the bounded repair policy was never invoked (repair_count = 0) and the preregistered secondary estimand (repair_success_rate—the fraction of initial-error tasks where the final config is validator-clean) is not empirically computable. Representative per-episode traces (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json sha256: 020baed3e0e4283cc5e25413af002166998bfc587a1919046ca53dab09251b30) confirm repair_applied = false and repair_prompt_sha256 = null.
sections.discussion: Artifact-grounded interpretation: Two immediate, artifact-grounded readings follow. First, under the shared_initial_generation contract and the synthetic 200-task corpus used here, the declared generator produced validator-clean candidates for every task; each per-episode validator_trace.validation_after.violation_count = 0. With no initial failures there was nothing for a bounded repair loop to correct, explaining the degenerate null. Second, because repairs were never invoked, the study provides no direct evidence about repair-strategy effectiveness when the generator proposes unsafe candidates. Design trade-offs and operational implications: The shared_initial_generation contract improves causal attribution but reduces sensitivity to generator stochasticity. In operational practice the value of verifier-in-the-loop architectures depends on (1) generator sampling dispersion (how often models propose unsafe candidates in the deployed prompt/temperature/settings), (2) validator fidelity to device/vendor semantics and production quirks, and (3) repair policy richness (single bounded repair vs iterative repair or multi-tool synthesis). The archived bundle allows controlled follow-ups that vary these axes. Reproducible follow-ups enabled by the archive: The submission archive contains the full task_manifest and raw responses so the following targeted studies can be run reproducibly without reauthoring task definitions: (A) switch to independent_condition_generation (two independent model calls per task) to increase baseline failure probability and allow repair opportunities; (B) increase repair budget and enable iterative repair strategies or multi-tool repair; (C) extend the validator harm-oracle to emulate vendor-specific quirks; and (D) inject adversarial prompt perturbations to measure robustness. Key reproducibility pointers: execution/task_manifest.jsonl (sha256: 4e8aa65489313209485a8492fb890be771570c0c487a6cb8da7b55db3fc1a39b) and execution/raw_results.jsonl (sha256: 9ec4eb2ce01f16d9eb0191b80eda199ec2655637aa2c6c775f8babb62962b46f).
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed, preregistered paired trial to measure the marginal effect of a deterministic Batfish-style validator in a bounded generate→validate→repair pipeline under a shared_initial_generation contract. For the supplied synthetic 200-task bank and declared generator (gpt-5-mini) the shared initial candidates were validator-clean on all tasks; both baseline and guarded arms were validator-clean on all tasks, producing an exact paired difference of 0.0 (95% CI [0.0,0.0]; McNemar p = 1.0). No repairs were invoked and thus repair efficacy was not observed. These artifact-grounded results do not disprove verifier-assisted workflows’ potential value; they demonstrate that preregistered contract choices (shared vs independent generation), task-bank challenge level, validator expressiveness, and repair policy jointly determine whether verifier assistance yields an observable benefit. The archived execution bundle contains the task manifest, raw responses, per-episode validator traces, paired contingency tables, and reconciliation logs necessary to reproduce the run and to run follow-ups that trade generator variance against repair opportunity to quantify repair-mediated gains in realistic settings.

limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to a synthetic public task corpus and a deterministic Batfish-style sandbox; results do not generalize to production devices, multi-vendor heterogeneity, or richer harm oracles.
Single declared model family tested (gpt-5-mini) and a single bounded repair budget (≤1 repair); no cross-model or multi-iteration repair claims are made.

The preregistered shared_initial_generation contract produced exactly one shared initial generation per task that was reused for both conditions; this reduces sensitivity to generator stochasticity and therefore reduced the likelihood of observing discordant pairs arising purely from generation variance.

The repair loop was never invoked because baseline produced zero validator-detected errors; therefore the preregistered secondary hypothesis about repair-success (>50%) could not be empirically evaluated.

Contamination and template-alignment risk: automated contamination checks recorded no flagged items, but pretraining memorization or template-alignment remains a construct-validity threat that automated checks cannot fully eliminate.
Adversarial and prompt-injection scenarios were not included; the study does not assess robustness under targeted attacks.
